name: Glutathione
short: Inhaled: major airway narrowing (FEV1 -19%) in a study of 8 people with mild asthma. Oral: tolerated in a 4-week trial; a review reports substantial adverse effects and calls IV use contraindicated.
text: Inhaled (nebulised): in a randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study in 8 people with mild asthma, 600 mg of nebulised glutathione caused major airway narrowing (FEV1 fell 19% from baseline, against 1% with placebo) and induced cough in four and breathlessness in three; salbutamol given beforehand blocked this, and the authors attributed it to sulfite formation. In contrast, in cystic fibrosis, a 6-month randomised placebo-controlled trial of inhaled glutathione in 153 people aged 8 and over found a similar adverse event incidence with glutathione and placebo, and a 12-month randomised trial in 54 adults and 51 children reported that inhaled glutathione was well tolerated by all patients. Oral: in a 4-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in 60 otherwise healthy medical students, 500 mg a day was very well tolerated, as was placebo, but the authors noted that long-term safety had not been established. A 2025 systematic review of glutathione for skin lightening paired minimal adverse effects with topical and substantial adverse effects with oral glutathione, without the abstract naming those effects, and stated that intravenous glutathione is contraindicated because of lack of efficacy and side effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
